mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7% for three consecutive months is associated with reduced consumer spending power, which depresses earnings for broad-market firms and results in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -4%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which lowers earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < 0% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% combined with a concurrent decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1% signals a policy-driven liquidity expansion, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.0% AND CPIAUCSL < 1.0% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 250k per month for three consecutive months signals a robust labor market expansion, which increases consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 250000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +4%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 3% month-over-month signals a sharp demand shock, which immediately depresses equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns within the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 m/m change < -3% AND HOUST m/m change < -3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 70% of triggered events.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.5% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +3%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes.
